_note: Vendored, not fetched. proofplane's evidence is hash-chained and regenerated nightly in CI;
a build that reached the network for these figures would make a reproducible artefact depend
on a third-party site being up. Refresh by hand from the source below and commit the change.
These are NOT the source of any figure in scenarios.json. They exist so a reviewer can check
the claim scenarios.json makes about itself: that its magnitudes are anchored on generic
breach-cost reporting rather than AI-specific data. Only magnitude is carried across.
Frequency is deliberately omitted - a per-firm annual breach rate and a per-workflow agent
event rate are not the same quantity and comparing them would be worse than not comparing.

lossTypes.label: US · United States Finance Business Email Compromise Midmarket
lossTypes.why: Fraudulent payment induced by deception. The nearest published analogue to an agent tricked into moving money.
lossTypes.notGoodFor: Benchmark-grade US BEC frequency, sector-specific severity, or tail-loss decisions.

sources.name: Verizon 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report
sources.limitation: Median of FBI IC3 complaint-reported BEC losses as presented by Verizon DBIR; complaint-driven and self-reported, not financial-services-specific or mid-market-specific, and not a formal minimum quantile for this scenario.

sources.name: FBI IC3 2025 Annual Report
sources.limitation: US IC3 complaint population; self-reported and complaint-driven; not financial-services-specific, mid-market-specific, or a full loss distribution.

sources.name: Coalition funds transfer fraud largest clawback case
sources.limitation: One documented extreme funds-transfer-fraud case from a cyber insurer's book, not a modeled loss percentile or a financial-services mid-market average; 85% was recovered via clawback in this instance, but recovery is not guaranteed, so the gross figure is modeled; BEC/FTF-specific but drawn from a single case. Revise when a US mid-market BEC loss distribution with tail quantiles is reviewed.

lossTypes.label: US · United States Finance Data Breach Midmarket
lossTypes.why: Unauthorised disclosure of records. The nearest published analogue to data leaving through an agent path.
lossTypes.notGoodFor: Treating the bridged UK frequency as a US per-firm breach rate, or using the enterprise IBM financial-services average as an expected mid-market loss.

sources.name: NetDiligence Cyber Claims Study 2025 (Fifteenth Annual)
sources.limitation: Insured-claim crisis-services subset; not full total loss; SME band is broad (under USD 2B revenue) and not isolated to financial services.

sources.name: NetDiligence Cyber Claims Study 2025 (Fifteenth Annual)
sources.limitation: Insured-claim sample: covers claims of USD 1K or more that reached an insurer, so it excludes uninsured, self-absorbed and unreported losses, and is censored by policy limits and self-insured retentions. The SME band spans revenue up to USD 2B even though the financial-services sample averages USD 113M. Pooled 2020-2024 in nominal dollars with no inflation adjustment. RiskShard's mid_market band is defined by headcount while this segmentation is by revenue - the mapping is an explicit assumption, not a measurement.

sources.name: NetDiligence Cyber Claims Study 2025 (Fifteenth Annual)
sources.limitation: A single observed claim, not a modeled percentile - it is the maximum of 579 claims over five years, so it says nothing about how much worse a loss could be, and a larger sample would likely show a larger maximum. Insured-claim basis, so it is censored by policy limits and excludes uninsured or unreported losses. The SME band spans revenue up to USD 2B. Nominal 2020-2024 dollars, not inflation-adjusted.
